findings: Grade each independent binary rubric question exactly once per intentional repeat_count slot; never place the same question twice in one batch; remix batch membership across repeats so co-occurrence is not a fixed confounder.
Failure repair overwrites the failed logical sample in the same repeat slot and lineage; it does not increment repeat_count or create a new draw.

Confidence-triggered retries are a separate lineage: they are not slot repairs, are not mixed at raw-label level with the primary series, and enter comparison only after each lineage has its own within-leaf reduction.
Canonical HBQ weights apply only to post-reduction leaf scores, never to raw YES/NO draws, repaired substitutes, or unreduced retry labels.

Use the same robust reducer family as aggregate scores: map YES=1 and NO=0; drop NA and CANNOT_ASSESS from the numeric set S; point estimate is mean(S) for n<4 and symmetric 1-high/1-low discard then mean of the remainder for n>=4.

Small-N: n=0 is non-numeric (see semantics); n=1 is identity; n=2 and n=3 are untrimmed means. Symmetric high/low discard is forbidden unless n>=4 so a 1+1 trim cannot collapse the leaf to a single leftover or silently become a median-of-3.

Emit min, max, and SD cards on the pre-trim valid set S (primary lineage after repairs, excluding NA/CANNOT_ASSESS). Cards are descriptive; they do not replace the robust point estimate and are omitted or marked undefined when n<2 for SD and n<1 for min/max.

Hard-gates reduce within-leaf first, then gate the parent: they are not compensable by HBQ-weighted credit. Default conservative gate: any NO in the reduced/applicable set fails; NA does not fire the gate; unresolved CANNOT_ASSESS after repair blocks pass (not a silent YES).
recommendations: Fix repeat_count as the number of intentional primary slots per question; implement batch builders that enforce uniqueness within a batch and shuffle grouping between repeats.
Classify every (re)grade as primary, repair, or confidence-retry before storage so reducers can refuse cross-lineage raw pooling.

Reduce each leaf with the shared robust rule, then apply HBQ weights and hard-gates only on those reduced values; compute overall score on weighted non-gate leaves and overall pass as (all hard-gates pass) AND (score vs threshold).

Keep NA out of numerator and denominator; treat CANNOT_ASSESS as missing evidence that may trigger repair or block a hard-gate, never as NO-equivalent in the mean unless a gate policy explicitly maps it after reduction.

For n>=4 always discard one highest and one lowest even when S is all 0s or all 1s (result unchanged, procedure deterministic); for binary ties, drop one instance of the extreme value. Do not increase trim width with n unless the aggregate-score family does the same.
Attach min/max/SD cards to each leaf for audit; use SD=0 and min=max when n>=2 and S is constant; do not use cards as weights or as a second score.
Document that majority-of-3 is not the small-N rule: n=3 stays an untrimmed mean to remain in the same family as large-N trimmed means and aggregate scores.
risks: Pooling confidence retries with primary raw labels inflates effective n, can trigger trim too early, and double-counts a single low-confidence attempt.
Applying HBQ weights before within-leaf reduction lets noisy repeats and repairs distort high-weight questions.
Trimming at n<4 makes the leaf estimator jumpy (binary 1+1 trim at n=3 leaves one vote) and breaks parity with aggregate-score reduction.
Treating NA as NO silently fails inapplicable items; treating CANNOT_ASSESS as YES lets hard-gates pass without evidence.
Hard-gates averaged into the weighted score allow low-weight failures to be offset; conversely, firing a gate on a single unrepaired parse failure confuses operational failure with a true NO.
Non-remixed batches can couple question-order or context effects across repeats, so repeat_count no longer estimates independent draws.
output.summary: Deterministic aggregation for independent binary rubric questions uses repeat_count as primary slots only: one grade per question per repeat, unique questions per batch, remixed batches across repeats. Repairs replace a failed slot; confidence retries are a separate lineage. Reduce each leaf first with the same robust family as aggregate scores (YES=1, NO=0, NA/CANNOT_ASSESS dropped; untrimmed mean for n<4; symmetric one-high/one-low discard then mean for n>=4), emit min/max/SD on pre-trim S, then apply canonical HBQ weights. Hard-gates are reduced within-leaf and then applied as non-compensable pass/fail (NO fails; NA ignored; unresolved CANNOT_ASSESS blocks).
